correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivative tests give the two conditional laws exactly. The quadratic energy derivative is \(a y^2(1-y^{2n})\), so stationarity with \(a\ne0\) yields \(\mathbb E[y^{2n+2}]=\mathbb E[y^2]\). Strict convexity gives the RMS ceiling; the endpoints are excluded by invariant-support dynamics except for the origin at zero. The second conditional law is an exact regression, and its residual is \(-\dot y\), yielding the variance decomposition by orthogonality. The sign-changing energy injection term forces positive mass on both sides of \(|y|=1\) for every non-origin stationary state. All algebraic identities were replayed with the packaged exact checker.

value.rationale: The threshold \(|y|=1\) is the intrinsic sign-change point of the generalized Rayleigh nonlinear damping, so a theorem resolving stationary mass on both sides of that threshold is directly tied to the mechanism of self-excitation rather than to an arbitrary statistic. The exact nonlinear regression identifies the deterministic damping curve as the conditional mean position at fixed velocity. The power-moment shell gives a parameter-independent RMS ceiling, yet the same balance proves that recurrent states must make excursions beyond that ceiling threshold. Together with the derivative-energy variance defect and exact zero covariance, these identities provide rigorous consistency tests for computed limit cycles across the entire generalized family.
